facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The main new debt is the $3.3bn 7.75% senior secured notes due 2031, issued by Core Scientific Finance I LLC at 99.25% and closed on 2026-05-06. facts.text: The structure protects noteholders for now but moves risk to the parent. The debt service reserve account of USD 347,900 thousand is 1.36x a year of coupon on the secured notes, and those notes sit in a ring-fenced subsidiary whose five subsidiary guarantors carry the notes' collateral. The parent gave an uncapped completion guarantee, so a delay or overrun is paid from parent cash that also has to support the revolver, and the notes begin to amortize only after rent commences, so FY2029 maturities of USD 649,750 thousand rest on an assumed first installment date. facts.label: Company description and ownership
facts.text: Core Scientific is a data-center operator that now earns most of its revenue from long-term colocation leases instead of bitcoin: colocation was 84% of nine-month revenue against 14% a year earlier, from 11 data centers in seven states. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are defensible because power and fuel pass through colocation customers without markup, so power prices change colocation revenue and cost equally. Colocation gross margin was 59.59% and operating margin 31.07% in the third quarter, but those margins include a pass-through and only two quarters at scale, and the mining segments still bear their own power cost until they end. Tariffs raise equipment cost on projects the customer does not fund, which now means the AMD and Neocloud build, so cost inflation falls on the company there. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is high and works through cost of capital and access to power: the company competes with large, well-capitalized data-center providers with a lower external cost of capital and with other former miners converting to colocation, so it cannot expect pricing power and its edge is speed of delivery and sites that already have power. Buyer power is very high because one customer supplies 93% of revenue, and the second customer group has not yet commenced. Supplier power is also high: utilities require collateral before delivering power, equipment lead times exceed 12 months and tariffs raise cost, which ties up cash and can delay lease commencement. New entrants face the same power constraint, which protects sites that already hold interconnection. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths are contracted lease payments, a reserve-backed secured bond, power pass-through and a rapid earnings ramp. Weaknesses are single-customer dependence, negative free cash flow, run-rate leverage of 6.55x net and an unremediated reporting weakness. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the AMD and Neocloud leases commencing from 2027, conversion of the 2029 convertible notes into equity and exercise of the Tranche 1 warrants. Threats that could weaken it are a stalled billing ramp, a failed project bond, a CoreWeave payment event and a fall in the share price that closes the revolver and the warrant cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 months the company has to bill the remaining contracted CoreWeave capacity, finish the hosted mining wind-down by 2026-12-31, raise project-level bond financing for the AMD and Neocloud build and see whether the Tranche 1 warrants are exercised by 2027-01-23, and each of these supports or pressures liquidity directly, and no credit facility expires in that period because they mature on 2029-08-25. Over the following years the AMD and Neocloud leases start from 2027, contracted lease payments rise to USD 666,494 thousand by 2030, the notes begin to amortize after rent commences and the 2031 maturities of USD 3,355,750 thousand fall due, so refinancing capacity depends on a larger earnings base by then. The company-specific tailwind is rent already contracted; the headwinds are tariffs, equipment lead times, utility collateral and one customer. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A plausible downside starts with a delay in equipment or construction that holds billing capacity near its present level while the AMD build proceeds on the company's own funding. The first operating break would be billing growth that stalls, delaying the cash that was meant to arrive as capacity converts; the financial transmission is that annualized Adjusted EBITDA of USD 534,272 thousand would still cover annual coupons 1.98x, but capital spending would continue, and unrestricted cash plus the undrawn revolver of USD 903,941 thousand is smaller than the USD 965,794 thousand by which unrestricted cash fell in the third quarter. The liquidity consequence is that the company would rely on the restricted-cash release, the Tranche 1 warrants and the project bond, and if the share price fell the revolver would close and the warrant cash would shrink, leaving the parent's uncapped completion guarantee as the channel through which the notes' projects would draw parent cash. Management levers are deferring AMD work not yet delivered, since vendor contracts can generally be cancelled before delivery, slowing land and power purchases, and replacing cash collateral with letters of credit; observable triggers are a missed bond window, falling billing capacity growth and cash approaching the USD 150.0 million minimum liquidity test. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Core Scientific presents an adequate but highly concentrated business profile supported by contracted lease payments, a reserve-backed secured bond and a fast earnings ramp, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, run-rate leverage of 6.55x net, reliance on one customer and an open reporting weakness. Cash-flow durability appears weak today and should improve as billing capacity and new leases arrive. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the project-level bond, the share price and the timely start of the AMD and Neocloud leases. The primary downside path is delay in delivery or financing while spending continues, which draws parent cash through the completion guarantee. Further analysis would require the executed leases, customer accounts, finance-group accounts and a cash flow forecast. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: delivery and funding of the contracted build-out. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C16

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage and interest cover cannot be measured on trailing earnings: reported EBITDA is negative for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, while USD 4,302,175 thousand of carrying-value debt, most of it issued in 2026, rests on contracted colocation capacity still being delivered.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; calculation K19; calculation K43

The latest quarter shows the ramp: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 133,568 thousand on revenue of USD 232,866 thousand covers the coupon interest of USD 67,388 thousand incurred in the quarter 1.98x, but the issuer added add-backs to Adjusted EBITDA during 2026, so no trailing figure is comparable. Net debt of USD 3,498,234 thousand counts only unrestricted cash; restricted cash adds USD 837,603 thousand, including a debt service reserve. The first coupon on the 2031 secured notes fell due on 2026-11-15, after the last document supplied.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation K29; calculation K5; calculation K31; calculation K41
### Credit analysis

Net debt rose by USD 2,749,287 thousand in nine months, from USD 748,947 thousand at 2025-12-31 to USD 3,498,234 thousand at 2026-09-30, because the 7.75% secured notes added USD 3,300,000 thousand of principal in May 2026 while the USD 1,000,000 thousand term loan drawn in March was repaid from the proceeds. The secured notes are three quarters of contractual principal, while at the end of 2025 all of the debt was convertible notes, so the debt now rests mainly on the completion and leasing of the data centres the secured notes fund.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation K44; calculation K2; calculation K43

Reported EBITDA, which the issuer does not print and which is derived here as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, is negative for FY2024, FY2025 and the twelve months to 2026-09-30, so total debt and net debt multiples are not calculable and the interest cover is negative. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, FY2024 shows total debt of 6.93x and net debt of 1.61x, but FY2025 is negative and the twelve months to 2026-09-30 are not comparable because the annual figure uses the earlier definition and the nine-month figures the wider one. Against that, contracted operating lease payments expected to be received total USD 7,484,422 thousand, before the leases that have not yet commenced.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation K19; calculation K27; calculation K28; calculation K12; calculation K11

Cash interest paid of USD 19,229 thousand over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 predates the first coupon on the secured notes, so it understates the burden: the annual coupons on the secured notes and the 2029 convertible notes are USD 269,550 thousand. Against the quarter's incurred coupon interest, Adjusted EBITDA gives 1.98x and reported EBITDA gives 1.34x; both are quarterly figures and are not annualised.
Basis: calculation K20; calculation K37; calculation K29; calculation K30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 22

Operating cash flow of USD 296,243 thousand for the nine months is not a clean measure of earnings power, because it includes USD 286,765 thousand of proceeds from selling bitcoin earned by self-mining, and the stock of bitcoin is now almost exhausted. Purchases of property, plant and equipment of USD 1,494,979 thousand alone exceeded operating cash flow, leaving free cash flow of negative USD 1,198,736 thousand before USD 676,881 thousand of land and power acquisitions, so the build-out is funded by the new debt rather than by operations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation K34; calculation K33

Customer prepayments are a non-debt funding float: deferred revenue stood at USD 573,571 thousand at 2026-09-30 against USD 555,851 thousand at 2025-12-31. It funds construction and unwinds as capacity is delivered, so it is an obligation to deliver rather than free cash; the documents read do not state refund terms if delivery slips.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; calculation K39; calculation K38; calculation K40

Liquidity is cash of USD 803,941 thousand plus an undrawn USD 100,000 thousand revolver, against restricted cash of USD 837,603 thousand held in utility and development escrows and the debt service reserve. Expected purchase and construction commitments are about USD 4.4 billion, substantially all within two years, and the company expects to issue project-level bonds within twelve months to fund part of the AMD and Neocloud build-out.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation K31

The main data-quality risks are that FY2024 was restated for improperly capitalised assets committed to demolition, that the control weakness behind it was unremediated at 2026-09-30, and that the 2026 statements are unaudited. The main definition risks are the Adjusted EBITDA change, three liquidity measures that differ across releases, and interest shown as expense, as incurred coupon and as cash paid. Each conflict is logged with both figures.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 72–74; EX99.1_2026-06-30_corz_q22026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-03-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 46; EX99.1_2026-03-31_corz_q12026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_corz_q22026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

No event after the balance-sheet date of 2026-09-30 is stated in the documents read, so no pro forma adjustment is made. Holders of the 2029 convertible notes could convert in the fourth quarter of 2026 because the share-price condition was met in each quarter of 2026, and none had elected to by 2026-09-30, so the 2029 maturity is not the only way those notes can leave the debt stack.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 26

## Gaps

- Reported EBITDA, derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, is negative for FY2024, FY2025 and the twelve months to 2026-09-30, so total debt and net debt multiples on reported EBITDA are not calculable and interest cover is negative; this restricts every leverage conclusion, it is a high-severity gap, and no action closes it until operating earnings turn positive.

- The twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA to 2026-09-30 is not comparable, because FY2025 is on the earlier definition, the nine-month figures are on the wider 2026 definition and no Q4 2025 figure on the wider definition is printed; this blocks a leverage multiple on the issuer's own measure, it is a high-severity gap, and the action is to obtain FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA on the 2026 definition.

- No standalone or restricted-group statements are supplied for Core Scientific Finance I LLC and its five subsidiary guarantors, so debt, cash and earnings are consolidated while the secured notes' covenants bind only that group; this restricts any coverage or structural conclusion for the notes, it is a high-severity gap, and the action is to obtain issuer-level accounts.

- Cash interest paid for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 predates the first coupon on the secured notes, so the cover for that period understates the interest burden; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to recompute cover once the first coupon, due 2026-11-15, is reported.

- Undrawn committed facilities are not supplied for the balance-sheet dates before 2026-09-30 because no source states one; this is a low-severity gap and the action is to confirm from later filings that none existed.

- Cells the filings print as a dash are shown as Not supplied rather than zero, as the method requires, so line-by-line sums are not checked for those columns; this is a low-severity gap with no action beyond reading the filings.

- The cash flow row for proceeds from sales of digital assets is printed with four figures for three columns in the 2025 annual report, so the FY2024 and FY2025 values are not supplied; this is a low-severity gap and the action is to check the filing's layout.

- The legal ranking of the revolver, the letter of credit facility and the two convertible notes against the secured notes is not stated in any document, so only the secured notes are ranked in the debt stack; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain the credit agreement and the indentures.

- The secured notes' amortisation in the maturity ladder assumes a first installment date of 2029-11-15 that the indenture makes contingent on rent commencement and the abatement of revenue credits, so the split between FY2029, FY2030 and FY2031 could move; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain the indenture's schedule.
- No balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is in the documents, so period-end balances cannot be shown for the nine months of 2025; this is a low-severity gap with no action.

- The 2024 statements were restated, and the amended 2024 annual report and the amended 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied, so FY2024 and the 2025 interim comparatives rest on the restated comparatives alone; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain the amended filings.

- Depreciation and amortization differs between the cash flow statement and the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation by USD 72 thousand for FY2025 and USD 95 thousand for Q1 2026, and the filings do not explain it; this is a low-severity gap and the cash flow figure is used.

- The 2029 convertible notes are convertible at holders' option during the fourth quarter of 2026, so their principal may leave the debt stack by conversion; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to monitor conversion notices.
- No document after 2026-11-05 is supplied, so the first coupon due 2026-11-15 and any later financing are not evidenced; this is a low-severity gap and the action is to read later filings.

- The quarterly statements are unaudited and the control weakness behind the 2024 restatement was unremediated at 2026-09-30, so property, plant and equipment and impairment figures carry restatement risk; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to read the annual assessment at 2026-12-31.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Core Scientific has become a single-customer data-center landlord, so creditors depend on CoreWeave paying and on contracted capacity being built and funded on time; no sponsor or controlling shareholder is named in the filings. One customer supplied 93% of third-quarter 2026 revenue and 84% of nine-month revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 74

The AMD and Neocloud leases signed in July 2026 are the only contracted diversification, and none had commenced by 2026-09-30. About $4.4bn of build commitments are only partly funded by customers, and an accounting control weakness that forced a restatement is still open.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 73
### Key findings

Customer concentration is the dominant business risk, and it is still rising. Colocation was 84% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 14% a year earlier, and CoreWeave is the only colocation customer. CoreWeave has assigned the Dalton 1 and Denton North license agreements to a special purpose subsidiary, which the company understands received customer commitments sufficient for investment-grade debt, while CoreWeave remains a primary obligor; the company still says its ability to enforce recourse would depend on CoreWeave's financial condition at the time of a default.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation M10; calculation M7

Delivery, not demand, is the nearer-term risk. Billing capacity covers 82.20% of the CoreWeave contract, the rest is still in construction, and the AMD and Neocloud leases would take contracted capacity to 1.90x the CoreWeave contract once built from 2027. Build commitments of $4.4bn are substantially all due within 24 months, and management expects project-level bond financing, warrant exercise proceeds and the release of restricted cash to cover what customers do not fund.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation B1; calculation B3

Diversification is real but partly paid for in equity and unproven on terms. AMD signed directly for 71.27% of the new capacity and has credit support agreements on the Neocloud leases that let it cure Neocloud defaults but do not oblige it to. AMD also received a warrant over 9.31% of current shares, valued at $296.4 million on issue and booked as a lease incentive that reduces recognized revenue over the lease terms, together with a right to reserve a further large block of capacity until 2028-12-28; the rent and termination rights of these leases are not disclosed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation B9; calculation B16

Ownership gives creditors neither a sponsor to rely on nor one to fear, but the equity overhang is large. The company is publicly held, has paid no dividends and reported no related-party transactions in 2024 or 2025. Warrants, convertible notes and the AMD warrant could add shares equal to 62.32% of those outstanding, and the Tranche 1 warrants, worth up to $646.27 million in cash if all are exercised, expire on 2027-01-23; the share price when the AMD warrant was set was $20.74, 3.05x their $6.81 strike.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation B4; calculation B8; calculation B10

Reporting quality is the weakest governance point. A material weakness over accounting for the demolition and impairment of converted mining facilities led to restated 2024 and 2025 interim statements and an adverse opinion on internal control for 2025, it was still unremediated on 2026-09-30, and the auditor changed in 2025. The 2024 net loss is larger after restatement than first reported, so property, plant and equipment and impairment figures carry further restatement risk.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 73

The secured notes sit in a ring-fenced finance subsidiary, not at the parent. Core Scientific Finance I LLC issued them, five operating subsidiaries guarantee them, and they are secured on those subsidiaries' assets and on the issuer's equity; Core Scientific, Inc. is not named as a guarantor but gave an uncapped completion guarantee for the financed projects. The proceeds left after the reserve account went to the parent, which repaid the $1.0bn term loan, so the notes' covenants constrain only the finance group. The new revolver and letter of credit facility are secured separately, on substantially all assets of the parent and its guarantors.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_corz_d149019dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 65

Access to the new revolver depends on the equity price. Each borrowing needs a market capitalization of at least $3,000 million, and the facilities require minimum liquidity of $150.0 million at each quarter end, so the revolver is least available if the shares fall at the time cash is needed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23

The restructuring history is recent and the business model is new. The company filed for Chapter 11 on 2022-12-21 and emerged on 2024-01-23, signed its first colocation contract in 2024, and mining fell to 7.49% of third-quarter 2026 revenue from 81.57% in the third quarter of 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation B11; calculation B12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is contract quality and early delivery. Current billing capacity supports, by management's own measure, over $700 million of annual colocation revenue, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA reached $133.6 million at a 57% margin, and CoreWeave has prepaid more than $570 million of deferred revenue, funded $180.9 million of 2026 capital spending and signed contracts of ten years or more. Contracted lease payments still to be received exceed $7bn on leases already commenced, with a further $1.8bn on CoreWeave leases not yet commenced. The company also holds more than $800 million of unrestricted cash, a $347.9 million reserve account and $600 million of new undrawn facilities, which gives time to deliver the remaining capacity.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation B18

The view would improve if the AMD and Neocloud leases commence on schedule from 2027 with their terms and credit support disclosed, if the project-level bond financing is completed, and if CoreWeave's share of revenue falls as the new leases bill. It would worsen on slippage in converting contracted capacity to billing, a late payment by or financial deterioration of CoreWeave, a further restatement, the Tranche 1 warrants lapsing unexercised, or a share price low enough to close the revolver.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49
### Limitations

- No executed CoreWeave, AMD or Neocloud lease is supplied, so termination rights and payment security are not stated and the rent of the AMD and Neocloud leases is unknown; the concentration conclusion could be firmer or weaker once those terms are read.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49

- The accounts and credit standing of CoreWeave and AMD, and the identity of the Neocloud counterparty, are not supplied, so the conclusion that creditor outcomes depend on CoreWeave paying cannot be sized for the likelihood of a payment failure, and the comfort from AMD's role cannot be weighed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49

- The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so directors, officers, holders above any ownership threshold and 2026 related-party matters are not established; the ownership conclusion rests on the record-holder count and the absence of a named sponsor, and would change if a large holder exists.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 154

- The Two Seas Capital cooperation agreement dated 2026-02-18 is known only as an exhibit title, so any investor influence on the board or strategy is not established; the no-controlling-holder view could change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 57

- Only some CoreWeave sites are named in the filings and the full list of five is not, so how much of the contracted rent sits at each project that secures the notes is not established; the conclusion on rent supporting the notes is directional only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-03-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX99.1_2026-03-31_corz_d149019dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The main new debt is the $3.3bn 7.75% senior secured notes due 2031, issued by Core Scientific Finance I LLC at 99.25% and closed on 2026-05-06. The company says the net proceeds funded a debt service reserve account and a distribution to the parent, which repaid and ended a $1.0bn 364-day term loan drawn in March 2026 in two steps of $500.0 million, the second after an amendment on 2026-03-18; that loan was secured on substantially all assets of the parent and its guarantors. $347.9 million remained in the reserve account on 2026-09-30. The notes are guaranteed by five subsidiaries that were the issuer's only subsidiaries at issue, secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the issuer and those guarantors and on the issuer's equity, and covered by an uncapped completion guarantee from Core Scientific, Inc. for specified data-center projects. Principal amortization begins only after rent commencement and the end of revenue credits to the tenant, at an initial 11.50% of original principal a year, and a first coupon was due on 2026-11-15.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_corz_d149019dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-03-31_corz_d47435dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-31_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 65

A $600.0 million credit agreement was signed on 2026-08-25, with a $100.0 million revolver and a $500.0 million letter of credit facility maturing on 2029-08-25, extendable to 2030-08-25; nothing was drawn on 2026-09-30. It is secured on substantially all assets of the parent and its guarantors, and requires minimum liquidity of $150.0 million at each quarter end and, for each revolver borrowing, a market capitalization of at least $3,000 million. The company expects to use letters of credit to replace cash collateral held for utility obligations and release about $300.0 million of restricted cash. Two convertible issues from 2024 also remain: $460.0 million of 3.00% notes due 2029, which holders may convert in the fourth quarter of 2026 because the share price trigger was met, and $625.0 million of 0.00% notes due 2031.

The company also issued AMD a warrant over up to 9.31% of current shares at $23.47 expiring 2031-07-27, with $296.4 million of fair value booked as a deferred lease incentive; AMD also holds a right to lease much more capacity until 2028-12-28. ## Gaps

- No executed CoreWeave, AMD or Neocloud lease is supplied, and no accounts or ratings of CoreWeave or AMD are supplied, so termination rights, payment security and the payment risk behind the largest revenue source are not sized; this is a high-severity gap and the action is to obtain the agreements and the customers' accounts.

- The terms, size and date of the project-level bond financing that management expects within twelve months are not stated, so the funding of the AMD and Neocloud build rests on an intention; this is a high-severity gap and the action is to read the financing when it is launched.

- The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so director and officer ownership, large holders and 2026 related-party matters are not established; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain it.
- The terms of the Two Seas Capital cooperation agreement are not described in the supplied text; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain the agreement filed in February 2026.
- Only some CoreWeave sites are named, so the share of contracted rent that supports the notes' collateral cannot be stated; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain a site schedule.

- The AMD warrant vests only as capacity is contracted and the rents of the AMD and Neocloud leases are not disclosed, so the full cost of the AMD contract is not established; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain the lease and warrant agreements.
- Fund vintage and sponsor exit pressure cannot arise because no sponsor is identified in the supplied documents; no action is needed unless a sponsor is found.
- No credit rating appears in the supplied documents; this is a low-severity gap and the action is to obtain rating reports if any exist.

- Where the filings and releases give different figures for one event, namely the Polaris price and the FY2024 net loss, all figures are kept and none is chosen; the Polaris difference of USD 1.9 million between the closing price and the signing price plus adjustments is not explained, and this is a low-severity gap.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Core Scientific's fundamental credit is weak today and depends on the build-out being completed and funded: reported EBITDA is negative, nine-month free cash flow is deeply negative, and net debt of USD 3,498,234 thousand rests on one customer's leases that are still being delivered.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C10

Contracted lease payments of USD 7,484,422 thousand on commenced leases, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 133,568 thousand and proven access to the secured bond market support debt service if delivery stays on schedule. About USD 4.4 billion of build commitments exceed the funding sources the company has identified, so the financing in the next twelve months decides the outcome.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C16
### Key findings

Leverage is high on every measure that can be calculated, and no trailing measure exists. Reported EBITDA is negative for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, and the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA cannot be compared over twelve months because its definition widened in 2026. Annualizing the third quarter's Adjusted EBITDA gives USD 534,272 thousand, against which net debt is 6.55x and contractual principal of USD 4,385,000 thousand is 8.21x, before the further borrowing the build-out needs; these are single-quarter run-rates on a company-defined measure, not trailing leverage.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

Free cash flow is deeply negative by design, and operating cash flow flatters it. Operating cash flow of USD 296,243 thousand included USD 286,765 thousand from selling bitcoin, so operations without those sales produced USD 9,478 thousand. Purchases of property, plant and equipment of USD 1,494,979 thousand left free cash flow at negative USD 1,198,736 thousand, and land and power purchases of USD 676,881 thousand took it to negative USD 1,875,617 thousand, so the build-out was paid for by new debt and by a fall of USD 965,794 thousand in unrestricted cash in the third quarter alone.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

Liquidity is thin against the commitments it must meet. Unrestricted cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 903,941 thousand, which is 20.54% of about USD 4.4 billion of purchase and construction commitments that fall substantially all within 24 months; adding an expected restricted-cash release, every Tranche 1 warrant being exercised and the amount passed through to CoreWeave still covers only 46.65%. The balance depends on the project-level bond financing that management expects within twelve months and whose terms are not stated.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16

Contracted rent is the main support, but its cushion over debt service is modest before operating costs. Lease payments to be received on commenced leases total USD 7,484,422 thousand and rise from USD 350,909 thousand in 2027 to USD 639,045 thousand in 2029, with a further USD 1.8bn on CoreWeave leases not yet commenced; the 2027 amount is 1.30x the annual coupons of USD 269,550 thousand and the 2028 amount is 1.67x, before power and operating costs, capital spending and the secured notes' amortization.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C7; calculation C19; calculation C20

The structure protects noteholders for now but moves risk to the parent. The debt service reserve account of USD 347,900 thousand is 1.36x a year of coupon on the secured notes, and those notes sit in a ring-fenced subsidiary whose five subsidiary guarantors carry the notes' collateral. The parent gave an uncapped completion guarantee, so a delay or overrun is paid from parent cash that also has to support the revolver, and the notes begin to amortize only after rent commences, so FY2029 maturities of USD 649,750 thousand rest on an assumed first installment date.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C18; calculation C31

Concentration is the dominant business risk and will fall only when the 2027 leases commence. One customer supplied 93% of third-quarter revenue and 84% of nine-month revenue, and the AMD and Neocloud leases that diversify it do not start before 2027. AMD signed directly for 71.27% of that new capacity and holds the right, but not the obligation, to cure Neocloud defaults, while CoreWeave moved two license agreements to a special purpose subsidiary that the company understands received customer commitments sufficient for investment-grade debt.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-03-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_corz.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C35; calculation C36

The earnings ramp is credible because power is passed through and margins are high. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 133,568 thousand was 3.25x the second quarter's, a margin of 57.36%, as billing capacity rose by 22.78%; colocation gross margin was 59.59% and operating margin 31.07%. The same quarter capitalized USD 17,774 thousand of interest, so reported interest expense of USD 54,066 thousand understates the USD 71,840 thousand incurred.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 50; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26

Refinancing capacity is real but depends on the equity price. The company priced USD 3.3 billion of secured notes at 7.75% in April 2026, and at the share price of USD 20.74 when the AMD warrant was set the 2029 convertible notes were 1.89x their conversion price, so conversion could remove USD 460,000 thousand of debt, while the 2031 convertible notes were at 0.92x. Revolver borrowing needs a market capitalization of at least USD 3,000 million, which on the current share count means a price of USD 9.31, 55.11% below that reference price, so the condition binds only in a sharp fall; the minimum liquidity test of USD 150,000 thousand has headroom of USD 753,941 thousand, and the Tranche 1 warrants expire on 2027-01-23.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C41

Governance is neutral for cash leakage and adverse for reporting quality. There is no named sponsor, no dividend and no related-party transaction in 2024 or 2025, but a material weakness that forced a restatement is unremediated, and warrants, convertible notes and the AMD warrant could add shares equal to 62.32% of those outstanding.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation C32
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a weak view is that the company has funded each large step so far and the contracts behind the build are long and customer-funded. CoreWeave funds almost all of its conversion projects with the company's contribution capped at a fixed amount, deferred revenue of USD 573,571 thousand is almost all CoreWeave prepayment, the secured notes closed with a reserve account, and unrestricted cash fell but still stood at USD 803,941 thousand, with an undrawn revolver and a letter of credit facility that is expected to release restricted cash. If the 2029 convertible notes convert, USD 460,000 thousand of debt becomes equity, and if the Tranche 1 warrants are exercised USD 646,269 thousand of cash arrives; together with the project bond these would close the gap.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation C33

The view would improve if the project-level bond is completed on stated terms, if billing capacity keeps rising toward the CoreWeave contract and the AMD and Neocloud leases commence in 2027, and if Adjusted EBITDA holds near the third-quarter run-rate for two or more quarters on a stable definition. It would worsen if financing slips while spending continues at the third-quarter pace, if CoreWeave pays late or its credit weakens, if a further restatement follows the open control weakness, or if the share price falls toward USD 9.31, where the revolver would close, or below the USD 6.81 exercise price of the Tranche 1 warrants.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49
### Limitations

- Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's own measure, widened in 2026, and no document gives a trailing twelve months on that definition, so the annualized leverage multiples show scale rather than a ratio that a covenant or agency would compute; a consistent definition could move them materially in either direction.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 10

- Neither a build schedule nor a cash flow forecast is supplied, so the funding gap is sized from the total of commitments against identified sources and not from a month-by-month profile; the liquidity conclusion could prove too severe if spending is later in the 24 months or too mild if costs rise.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 53

- Cash flow statements are printed only for nine months, so the third-quarter cash movement is inferred from balance sheets; the free cash flow conclusion for the latest quarter alone is therefore not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 7

- No peer, market price or rating information is supplied, so the business and financial profile is judged against the company's own history and statements rather than against comparable issuers, and the Average assessments could be too generous or too harsh.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 53

- The share price after 2026-07-27 is not supplied, so whether the convertible notes, the warrants and the revolver condition stand in the money or in range today is not established, and the refinancing conclusion rests on a price about four months old.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 28
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is contracted visibility: lease payments to be received on commenced leases of USD 7,484,422 thousand, on terms of ten years or more, give a floor under revenue that a mining business never had, and they rise each year to 2030, which supports debt service and lowers the chance that the secured notes depend on market sentiment alone.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 48; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second strength is a demonstrated ability to raise secured debt at scale: USD 3.3 billion of notes priced at 7.75% in April 2026 with a reserve account holding 1.36x a year of coupon, which shortens the period in which noteholders are exposed to a missed completion milestone.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_corz_d47435dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C18

The third strength is a fast earnings ramp on a passed-through power model: third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 133,568 thousand at a margin of 57.36% shows that billing capacity converts to earnings, and the customer funds most of the CoreWeave conversion cost, which limits the company's own capital at risk there.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_corz_q32026corescientificinc-ea-htm.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C22; calculation C23

The fourth strength is optionality in the equity-linked instruments: the 2029 convertible notes can leave the debt stack by conversion, and the Tranche 1 warrants can bring cash, which reduces the gross funding needed from lenders if the share price holds.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C27; calculation C33

The first weakness is single-customer dependence: 93% of third-quarter revenue and the whole colocation line come from one counterparty, so a payment or credit event at CoreWeave would reach revenue, prepayments and the secured notes' collateral at once.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C35

The second weakness is negative free cash flow and a funding gap: free cash flow was negative USD 1,198,736 thousand before land and power purchases, and identified sources cover 46.65% of about USD 4.4 billion of commitments, so completion depends on capital markets and the share price.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C10; calculation C16

The third weakness is leverage with no trailing earnings base: reported EBITDA is negative over twelve months and the run-rate multiples of 6.55x net and 8.21x on principal leave little room for a delay, since stockholders' deficit of USD 1,092,078 thousand also means there is no book equity cushion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C34

The fourth weakness is reporting quality: the control weakness behind the restatement of 2024 and 2025 interim statements is unremediated, so property, plant and equipment and impairment figures that underpin the collateral and earnings carry further restatement risk.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 73; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth weakness is structural and equity-price dependence: the revolver needs a market capitalization of at least USD 3,000 million for each borrowing, the parent's completion guarantee is uncapped, and the notes' covenants bind only the finance group, so creditors outside it rely on parent liquidity that the guarantee can consume.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; Business & governance (CP-1A)

### Company description and ownership

Core Scientific is a data-center operator that now earns most of its revenue from long-term colocation leases instead of bitcoin: colocation was 84% of nine-month revenue against 14% a year earlier, from 11 data centers in seven states. The company emerged from Chapter 11 on 2024-01-23, is widely held with no named sponsor or controlling holder, pays no dividend, and reported no related-party transactions in 2024 or 2025, so ownership neither supports nor extracts cash and the creditor case rests on the leases and the structure. The secured notes sit in a ring-fenced finance subsidiary with five guarantors, while the parent carries the convertible notes, the revolver and the completion guarantee.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 45
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is shifting from a price-driven commodity to contracted capacity, and growth now comes from converting contracted capacity into billing rather than from price. Colocation contracts run ten years or more with fixed payments on capacity plus variable payments, CoreWeave receives build credits during the initial billing period that defer cash against revenue, and billing capacity rose 22.78% in the third quarter while mining fell to 7.49% of revenue. Pricing power cannot be assessed, because the rent of the AMD and Neocloud leases and the per-unit rent of the CoreWeave leases are not disclosed, and revenue is concentrated in one customer.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation C24; calculation C37
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are defensible because power and fuel pass through colocation customers without markup, so power prices change colocation revenue and cost equally. Colocation gross margin was 59.59% and operating margin 31.07% in the third quarter, but those margins include a pass-through and only two quarters at scale, and the mining segments still bear their own power cost until they end. Tariffs raise equipment cost on projects the customer does not fund, which now means the AMD and Neocloud build, so cost inflation falls on the company there.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C25; calculation C26
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Earnings do not yet convert to free cash flow because capital intensity is at its peak. Nine-month purchases of property, plant and equipment of USD 1,494,979 thousand and land and power purchases of USD 676,881 thousand exceeded operating cash flow, interest capitalized of USD 17,774 thousand in the third quarter hides part of the coupon burden, and the annual coupon on the secured notes of USD 255,750 thousand is joined by amortization of USD 379,500 thousand a year once rent commences. Capital spending is flexible only in part: CoreWeave projects are customer-funded and capped, and vendor contracts can generally be cancelled before delivery, but the company has signed leases that require the AMD and Neocloud build.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C21; calculation C29; calculation C30
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is high and works through cost of capital and access to power: the company competes with large, well-capitalized data-center providers with a lower external cost of capital and with other former miners converting to colocation, so it cannot expect pricing power and its edge is speed of delivery and sites that already have power. Buyer power is very high because one customer supplies 93% of revenue, and the second customer group has not yet commenced. Supplier power is also high: utilities require collateral before delivering power, equipment lead times exceed 12 months and tariffs raise cost, which ties up cash and can delay lease commencement. New entrants face the same power constraint, which protects sites that already hold interconnection.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 53
### Macro and policy factors

Tariffs and utility interconnection rules are material for cost and timing and are covered above; other political, economic, social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_corz.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are contracted lease payments, a reserve-backed secured bond, power pass-through and a rapid earnings ramp. Weaknesses are single-customer dependence, negative free cash flow, run-rate leverage of 6.55x net and an unremediated reporting weakness. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the AMD and Neocloud leases commencing from 2027, conversion of the 2029 convertible notes into equity and exercise of the Tranche 1 warrants. Threats that could weaken it are a stalled billing ramp, a failed project bond, a CoreWeave payment event and a fall in the share price that closes the revolver and the warrant cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are Average: the company controls about 1.7 GW of leasable power across 11 sites, but only a part is billing and its rivals are better capitalized. Competitive advantage is Average: speed of conversion and powered sites are evidenced, while rent and pricing are not. Business diversification is Weak at 93% of revenue from one customer. Cost and capex flexibility is Average: power is passed through and customer-funded projects are capped, but commitments are large. Margin stability is Average: margins are high but proven for two quarters. Free cash flow stability is Weak: free cash flow is negative USD 1,198,736 thousand before land and power. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average: USD 3.3 billion of secured notes closed at 7.75%, yet the next financing is not yet raised and depends on the share price. Liquidity is Average and falling: USD 803,941 thousand of unrestricted cash and USD 100,000 thousand undrawn, with USD 753,941 thousand of headroom over the minimum liquidity test, against about USD 4.4 billion of commitments. Financial policy and governance is Average: no sponsor, no dividend and no related-party dealings offset an open reporting weakness and an uncapped parent guarantee. Trend is improving in earnings and worsening in leverage and funding need.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C39
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 months the company has to bill the remaining contracted CoreWeave capacity, finish the hosted mining wind-down by 2026-12-31, raise project-level bond financing for the AMD and Neocloud build and see whether the Tranche 1 warrants are exercised by 2027-01-23, and each of these supports or pressures liquidity directly, and no credit facility expires in that period because they mature on 2029-08-25. Over the following years the AMD and Neocloud leases start from 2027, contracted lease payments rise to USD 666,494 thousand by 2030, the notes begin to amortize after rent commences and the 2031 maturities of USD 3,355,750 thousand fall due, so refinancing capacity depends on a larger earnings base by then. The company-specific tailwind is rent already contracted; the headwinds are tariffs, equipment lead times, utility collateral and one customer.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 52
### Downside scenario

A plausible downside starts with a delay in equipment or construction that holds billing capacity near its present level while the AMD build proceeds on the company's own funding. The first operating break would be billing growth that stalls, delaying the cash that was meant to arrive as capacity converts; the financial transmission is that annualized Adjusted EBITDA of USD 534,272 thousand would still cover annual coupons 1.98x, but capital spending would continue, and unrestricted cash plus the undrawn revolver of USD 903,941 thousand is smaller than the USD 965,794 thousand by which unrestricted cash fell in the third quarter. The liquidity consequence is that the company would rely on the restricted-cash release, the Tranche 1 warrants and the project bond, and if the share price fell the revolver would close and the warrant cash would shrink, leaving the parent's uncapped completion guarantee as the channel through which the notes' projects would draw parent cash. Management levers are deferring AMD work not yet delivered, since vendor contracts can generally be cancelled before delivery, slowing land and power purchases, and replacing cash collateral with letters of credit; observable triggers are a missed bond window, falling billing capacity growth and cash approaching the USD 150.0 million minimum liquidity test.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_corz.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C12; calculation C13
### Overall credit view

Overall, Core Scientific presents an adequate but highly concentrated business profile supported by contracted lease payments, a reserve-backed secured bond and a fast earnings ramp, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, run-rate leverage of 6.55x net, reliance on one customer and an open reporting weakness. Cash-flow durability appears weak today and should improve as billing capacity and new leases arrive. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the project-level bond, the share price and the timely start of the AMD and Neocloud leases. The primary downside path is delay in delivery or financing while spending continues, which draws parent cash through the completion guarantee. Further analysis would require the executed leases, customer accounts, finance-group accounts and a cash flow forecast. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: delivery and funding of the contracted build-out.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C16

## Gaps

- No executed CoreWeave, AMD or Neocloud lease and no accounts or ratings of the customers are supplied, so the payment risk behind the main revenue source and the durability of rent are not sized; this is a high-severity gap and the action is to obtain the agreements and the customers' accounts.

- No build schedule or cash flow forecast is supplied, so the funding gap rests on total commitments against identified sources and not on timing; this is a high-severity gap and the action is to obtain the construction and funding plan.

- The terms, size and date of the project-level bond financing are not stated, so the main source of funds for the AMD and Neocloud build is an intention; this is a high-severity gap and the action is to read the financing when it launches.

- No accounts of the finance subsidiary and its guarantors are supplied, so cash generation and cover at the notes' issuer cannot be separated from the group; this is a medium-severity gap and the action is to obtain issuer-level accounts.
